findings.counterexample: Reproduced: repo/.git + repo/.totem/orchestration/totem-claude + stray repo/packages/cli/.totem/temp; a send from repo/packages/cli/src wrote to packages/cli/.totem/orchestration/totem-claude/outbox/ with verify.ok === true. findings.claim: ADR-106 line 150 tolerates a subject-only dispatch; the listing line called that class a transport drop and the refusal conflicts with the convention.
findings.counterexample: A subject-only dispatch reads bodyEmpty: true; the #2118 tests do not pin it.

findings.claim: The strip compared the raw slug while the filename is composed from the slugified one, so a spaced or underscored recipient prefix still doubled the recipient.
findings.counterexample: Reproduced: --slug 'Strategy Claude review' and 'strategy_claude-review' each wrote <stamp>-strategy-claude-strategy-claude-review with 0 warnings.

findings.claim: verify resolved its roster from the cwd's repository, not the file's.
findings.counterexample: From a marker-less cwd the resolver falls back to the cwd itself and the roster comes from the wrong tree (attested; on this host the walk climbed to the temp-dir .totem).

findings.claim: verifyDispatch inside mailSend could throw after the rename landed, so exit 1 would say nothing about the dispatch being written and a reply would skip its consume-mark.
findings.counterexample: Attested: the only throw is the readFileSync catch; a transient Windows lock reaches it.

findings.claim: verifyDispatch reads the whole file, so a file whose delimiter is inside the window but whose content past 16 KiB is only whitespace reads as non-empty.
findings.counterexample: Holds with a negligible edge; the bounded-read path is conservative and correct.

findings.claim: The sender token in position three does not disturb the positional recipient match or the #2311 sensor; no consumer parses basenames positionally; doctrine says seat-short where the mechanism uses the full id; a blank --slug silenced both the token and the slug.
findings.counterexample: Holds (hasSelfToken anchors on the stamp prefix; the sensor keys on exact basenames). The nit reproduced.

findings.claim: The three cases that pass on base are same-on-base locks; the skipIf is honest on CI but blind on this host; no Commander-level coverage for verify or reply --slug.
findings.counterexample: Holds.

findings.claim: The spec's correction block overcounted confabulations, left the realpath trap unanswered and drew only a test lesson from the ceiling-less walker.
findings.counterexample: Holds.

findings.claim: A worktree (a .git FILE) with a seat directory registered there gets the send, verify calls it routable, and no poll reads it; the hosting refusal's own hint (totem seat add) leads there.
findings.counterexample: Reproduced: a fixture with .git as a file and .totem/orchestration/totem-claude/ gave verify.ok true and the recipient poll saw nothing.

findings.claim: A reply with --slug <recipient> does not gain the sender token after the strip empties the slug, so two seats converge on one basename (the mmnto-ai/totem#2929 class).
findings.counterexample: Reproduced: totem-claude and totem-gemini both wrote 2026-09-23T0152Z-strategy-claude-re-kit-round.md.

findings.claim: Pre-existing: mail send --workspace and mail reply --workspace are claimed by the parent mail command and silently dropped; verify's optsWithGlobals read holds.

findings.claim: verify's findings no longer followed the documented order (parse, recipient, body, placement).
findings.counterexample: Reproduced: a phantom-placed file with a bad to: and an empty body gave [placement, recipient, body].

findings.claim: Segment arithmetic holds for POSIX, drive and UNC paths; a repository at a drive root or the POSIX root loses its separator; on a phantom the roster derived from the phantom's parent; the seat-directory test was always true.
findings.counterexample: Simulated with path.win32; the drive-root case gives repoOfFile 'D:' and path.resolve reads the per-drive cwd.

findings.claim: Claim 1 edges hold: D:/Dev refused; the .totem/temp start walks up; a start that is .totem itself lands at the root; .git-only refused; seat add creates the directory the hosting check reads; a submodule with .totem and a seat dir is the F1 shape.
findings.counterexample: Measured on this host except the submodule case (read from code).

findings.claim: The post-write verify try/catch has no lock.
findings.counterexample: grep for the finding text finds no test.

findings.claim: Changeset bullet 1 and spec item 3 matched the code, but 'a worktree is refused' held only while the worktree had no seat directory.

findings.claim: A repository with a .git directory that is not a direct child of the workspace (a clone elsewhere, or one nested inside a resident) takes a certified send the recipient's poll never lists, because enumerateOutboxes reads only the workspace's direct children.
findings.counterexample: Reproduced end to end with TOTEM_WORKSPACE=<tmp>/ws: <tmp>/elsewhere/clone and <tmp>/ws/totem/vendor/inner both gave verify.ok true and the poll missed them.

findings.claim: The roster-on-phantom lock passed on the pre-fix code because the static cohort map already carried the recipient; it locked nothing.
findings.counterexample: knownCohortAgents always seeds COHORT_AGENT_MAP, which holds strategy-claude.

findings.claim: A resident whose .totem is a junction or symlink gets a certified send no poll reads: the send and verify followed links, the reader never does.
findings.counterexample: Reproduced: <tmp>/ws/symrepo with .totem junctioned to <tmp>/realtotem gave verify.ok true and the poll missed it.

findings.claim: The resolver's doc comment still said a worktree's .git file counts, which the code below refuses.
findings.counterexample: Stale doc.

findings.claim: The senderInSlug doc said mailReply sets it only when no explicit slug is given; mailReply now always passes true and mailSend judges after the strip. Behaviour correct; no other caller exists; a plain send gets no token.
findings.counterexample: Stale doc.

findings.claim: Submodules and stray .git files were refused under the word worktree; refusing is right, the label was wrong. Relative, CRLF and backslash pointers resolve to the resident; a POSIX pointer at the filesystem root weakens only the hint.
findings.counterexample: gitdir: ../../.git/modules/x and a non-pointer file both read 'is a worktree'.

findings.claim: A .git symlink or junction to a directory is accepted as a resident checkout; the poll reads it, and the existsSync-then-statSync race errors loudly rather than certifying.
findings.counterexample: Reproduced: the poll lists a dispatch under a junctioned .git.
